The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange is opening its infrastructure to AI agents. Binance launched Agent OS, a platform that lets developers connect AI applications to analyze markets and execute trades on users' behalf—bringing autonomous AI directly into the business of managing real money.

The platform provides access to Binance's suite of tools including APIs, Wallet Agentic Hub, x402 transaction verification, and Skill Hub. It also supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling integration with popular developer tools like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex, Anthropic's Claude Code, and Cursor. Users can authorize agents to access market data, view account information, and execute trades autonomously.

The launch represents a significant shift in the AI agent landscape. While the industry has focused on chatbots that answer questions, the move toward action-capable agents is accelerating. Binance is positioning itself at the intersection of these two trends.

"Instead of total freedom, we put the power in users' hands to give them granular access control of what they can do through the agent," said Jeff Li, vice president of product at Binance. Security centers on subaccounts—users can assign specific permissions to agents for spot or futures trading, with withdrawals blocked by default. Users decide whether agents need approval for every order or can trade autonomously once configured.

The exchange does not impose separate caps on agent trading volumes; the amount users transfer into subaccounts effectively serves as the limit. Daily limits apply to the Agentic Wallet: $50,000 for regular swaps, $100,000 for DeFi transactions, and $20 for x402 payments.

Binance can monitor an agent's trading activity but has limited visibility into the reasoning behind trades—which happens either on the user's machine or within their chosen AI application. The company points to subaccounts as the primary defense against prompt injection attacks or other compromises.

The crypto exchange isn't alone in this space. Kraken launched an open source command-line tool with MCP support in March, allowing AI agents to execute trades. Coinbase followed with "Coinbase for Agents" in June, and OKX enabled agentic trading through an MCP toolkit earlier this year.
